HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MANOJ KUMAR GARG Judgment 15/05/2024

The petitioner has filed the present criminal revision petition being aggrieved by the judgment dt. 02.12.2004 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge (FT)
No.1, Sirohi in Sessions Case No. 116/2004 whereby, the learned Judge acquitted the respondents from offence under Section 498A and Section 306 IPC.

Briefly, the facts of the case are that the complainant petitioner lodged a report before the Superintendent of Police, Sirohi stating therein that his sister Chothi was married to accused Kasna about five years back.
Soon after marriage, she was subjected to cruelty by respondent husband and his family [2024:RJ-JD:22170] (2 of 7) [CRLR-926/2004] members.
On 20.09.2004, she has been killed by the respondents giving it a colour of suicide.
On the basis of said complaint, FIR was registered and investigation commenced.
The police after due investigation, filed challan against the respondents for offence under Section 498A and 306 IPC.
Thereafter, charges of the case were framed for aforesaid offences.
The accused respondents denied the charges and claimed trial.

1
The prosecution in support of its case examined seven witnesses and various documents were exhibited.
The statement of accused under Section 313 Cr.P.C. was recorded, who did not produce any witness in his defence.
After conclusion of trial, the trial court acquitted the respondents from offence under Section 498A and 306 IPC.
Learned counsel for the petitioner argued that the Court below without going through the entire record and evidence acquitted the respondents.
It is submitted that the prosecution witnesses Kala PW/2, Neti PW/3, Gwari PW/4 and Jamana PW/7 have stated that the deceased was subjected to cruelty soon before death.
However, the trial court acquitted the respondents on the basis of minor contradictions in the statement of the witnesses.

It is argued that the cumulative behaviour of the accused respondents towards the deceased compelled the deceased to commit suicide but the learned trial court ignored the evidence brought on record which resulted into erroneous acquittal of the accused respondents.
Thus the judgment of the Court below is liable to be set aside and the matter may be [2024:RJ-JD:22170] (3 of 7) [CRLR-926/2004] remanded back to the trial court for passing fresh order.

Per contra, counsel for the respondent accused argued that the prosecution primarily relied upon the statement of witnesses whose statements did not inspire confidence and they being full of contradictions.

In order to bring home the conviction for the offence under Section 306, IPC, the evidence of abetment by the accused respondent would have to be viewed in the light of the provisions of Section 107, IPC.
It is submitted that in the present case, Clause (1) of Section 107 IPC alone is applicable and the prosecution failed to prove that the respondent had instigated the deceased to commit suicide.
Therefore, no interference is called for in the impugned judgment and the appeal is liable to be dismissed.
I have heard the counsels for the parties and gone through the material on record.

From the evidence on record so also finding arrived by the learned courts below, it appears that the accused respondents have been acquitted on the ground that the prosecution has failed to prove its case against the respondents for offence under Section 498A and 306 IPC.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Ude Singh & Ors. Vs. State of Haryana reported in 2019 17 SCC 301, has held that in cases of alleged abetment of suicide, there must be a proof of direct or indirect act/s of incitement to the commission of suicide.

entities.text: Ude Singh & Ors. Vs. State of Haryana reported in 2019 17 SCC 301
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It could hardly be disputed that the question of cause of a suicide, particularly in the context of an offence of abetment of suicide, [2024:RJ-JD:22170] (4 of 7)
] remains a vexed one, involving multifaceted and complex attributes of human behavior and responses/reactions.
In the case of accusation for abetment of suicide, the Court would be looking for cogent and convincing proof of the act/s of incitement to the commission of suicide.

In the case of suicide, mere allegation of harassment of the deceased by another person would not suffice unless there be such action on the part of the accused which compels the person to commit suicide and such an offending action ought to be proximate to the time of occurrence.

Whether a person has abetted in the commission of suicide by another or not, could only be gathered from the Kala vs Kasna And Ors (2024:Rj-Jd:22170) on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198826372/
2 facts and circumstances of each case.

Aforesaid proposition of law taken into consideration clearly reveals that mere allegation of harassment of deceased by the accused named in the FIR may not be sufficient to conclude guilt, if any, under Section 306 IPC, rather to bring the accused in the ambit of 306 IPC, it is required to be established on record that deceased committed suicide after being instigated and abetted by the accused, which in the case at hand is totally missing.

Recently, Hon'ble Apex Court in case tilted Mariano Anto Bruno and another versus The inspector of Police, reported in 2022 Live Law(SC)834, held that not only there has to be evidence of continuous harassment, but there should be cogent evidence to establish a positive action by the accused which should more or less be proximate to the time of occurrence, which action can be said to have led or compelled the person to commit [2024:RJ-JD:22170] (5 of 7) [CRLR-926/2004]
suicide.

entities.text: Mariano Anto Bruno and another versus The inspector of Police, reported in 2022 Live Law(SC)834,
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It would be profitable to reproduce para No.34 of aforesaid judgment herein:-

"34. A bare perusal of the impugned judgment indicates that the High Court erred in recording the finding that there is sufficient evidence for convicting the appellants under Section 306 IPC losing sight of the fact that there exists no evidence on record indicating that the deceased was meted out with harassment by the appellants just before her death.
It is well-settled that not only there has to be evidence of continuous harassment, but there should be cogent evidence to establish a positive."
It has thus been observed that though presumption could be drawn, the burden of proof of showing that such an offence has been committed by the accused is on the prosecution.
The prosecution has to establish beyond reasonable doubt that the accused had instigated, conspired or intentionally aided so as to drive the wife to commit suicide.

In the instant case, the trial court while acquitting the accused respondent has observed that the prosecution witnesses are tutored witnesses spelling out similar statement but were not able to answer the questions which were put to them in cross- examination.

Thus, there is no evidence that deceased was meted with harassment for demand of dowry by the accused just prior to her death and she was instigated /abetted to commit suicide and as such, no case under S.498A and 306 IPC is made out.

In the opinion of this Court, the findings given by the trial Court are [2024:RJ-JD:22170]
(6 of 7) [CRLR-926/2004] perfectly justified and there is no illegality in the judgment of acquittal by the trial Court.

In the case of 'Mrinal Das & others v. The State of Tripura, :
2011(9) SCC 479,' decided on September 5, 2011, the Hon'ble Supreme Court, after looking into many earlier judgments, has laid down parameters, in which interference can be made in a judgment of acquittal, by observing as under:
"An order of acquittal is to be interfered with only when there are "compelling and substantial reasons", for doing so.

Mrinal Das & others v. The State of Tripura, :
2011(9) SCC 479
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
If the order is "clearly unreasonable", it is a Kala vs Kasna And Ors (2024:Rj-Jd:22170) on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198826372/
3 compelling reason for interference.

When the trial Court has ignored the evidence or misread the material evidence or has ignored material documents like dying declaration/report of ballistic experts etc., the appellate court is competent to reverse the decision of the trial Court depending on the materials placed.

Similarly, in the case of State of Rajasthan v. Shera Ram alias Vishnu Dutta, reported (2012) 1 SCC 602,' the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed as under:--
"A judgment of acquittal has the obvious consequence of granting freedom to the accused.

entities.text: State of Rajasthan v. Shera Ram alias Vishnu Dutta, reported (2012) 1 SCC 602
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This Court has taken a consistent view that unless the judgment in appeal is contrary to evidence, palpably erroneous or a view which could not have been taken by the court of competent jurisdiction keeping in view the settled canons of criminal jurisprudence, this Court shall be reluctant to interfere with such judgment of acquittal."
[2024:RJ-JD:22170] (7 of 7)
] There is a very thin but a fine distinction between an appeal against conviction on the one hand and acquittal on the other.

The preponderance of judicial opinion is that there is no substantial difference between an appeal against acquittal except that while dealing with an appeal against acquittal the Court keeps in view the position that the presumption of innocence in favour of the accused has been fortified by his acquittal and if the view adopted by the trial Court is a reasonable one and the conclusion reached by it had grounds well set out on the materials on record, the acquittal may not be interfered with.
Learned counsel for the appellant has failed to show any error of law or on facts on the basis of which interference can be made by this Court in the judgment under challenge.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, the present petition has no substance and the same is hereby dismissed.
The record of the trial court be sent back forthwith.

(MANOJ KUMAR GARG),J 25-BJSH/-
